open_points: Faults 1 and 2 (CHK-010, CHK-011) are both real and have the same cause. Spec 10.6 defines the write block term as only 'o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0', and spec 10.7, REQ-SRST-006 and SF-10.7-07 say the FIFO is ready for writes when busy = 0 and i_rst_n_sw = 1. The fix removes reg_sw_rst_pend from w_block in m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv. Nothing else changed. o_full, o_full_thr, the write acceptance and o_overflow now all follow the spec's block term, so CHK-010 and CHK-011 should both pass.

Spec 10.7 / REQ-SRST-008, pending request: the pending flop still moves the write FSM from RUN to REQ, so a request that arrives during a sequence is still served as a new sequence. In that one RUN cycle (busy = 0, i_rst_n_sw = 1) a write is accepted if o_full allows it, and an overflow pulse is raised if the FIFO is full. The new sequence then discards the word. The spec does not say whether a pending request should block writes in that RUN cycle. The approved decision on SF-3-47/SF-10.7-10 says tests must not rely on how pending pulses are remembered. I followed the literal block definition of 10.6, which is the reading the fault report asks for.

Pending request and the read side: in the pending case the request flop rises at the same write edge as a write-pointer increment. This is safe. The read side blocks as soon as it sees the request, which is no later than it sees the new write pointer. The write FSM resets the pointer in PTR, and the flush checks still wait for both pointers to be 0. Normal requests already behave the same way when a write was accepted in the cycle just before i_rst_n_sw falls.

fixes.spec_says: spec:527 (10.6, write domain): "block | o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0". spec:534 "o_full | block OR full flop". spec:535 "o_full_thr | if block: (i_full_thr equals 0), otherwise the full-threshold flop" (SF-10.6-03). spec:565 "The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1" (SF-10.7-07, also in REQ-SRST-006 spec:154, SF-3-45). spec:243 o_sw_rst_busy: "writes are possible again when it is 0". spec:142 REQ-IF-002: o_full is a flop "combined with the software reset block term by one gate". spec:134 REQ-FUNC-004 allows o_full=1 while a place is free only "because the freed place is not yet visible in the write domain". On the other side, spec:156 REQ-SRST-008 requires the pending request to be served from RUN, but it does not add it to the block term.
fixes.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:135 `assign w_block = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw | reg_sw_rst_pend;`, with the comment at :134 "A pending new request (REQ-SRST-008) also blocks in its RUN cycle". :285 `o_full = w_block | reg_full`. So at col9, with busy=0, i_rst_n_sw=1 and an empty FIFO (reg_full=0), o_full=1 only because reg_sw_rst_pend=1. That is a third block term that the spec does not define. :139 also rejects any write in that cycle.

fixes.spec_says: spec:138 REQ-FUNC-008: o_overflow is a one-cycle pulse "in the cycle after a write was requested while o_full was 1 and writes were not blocked by the software reset". spec:536 "o_overflow | flop: i_wr_en AND NOT block AND full flop, one cycle later" (SF-10.6-04). spec:527 block = "o_sw_rst_busy flop OR i_rst_n_sw = 0". spec:534 o_full = block OR full flop. spec:150 REQ-SRST-002 "A blocked write shall not raise o_overflow". spec:565 "The FIFO is ready for writes when o_sw_rst_busy is 0 and i_rst_n_sw is 1". spec:156 REQ-SRST-008, the pending request served from RUN.
fixes.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_sfifo_wr.sv:135 w_block includes reg_sw_rst_pend. :285 o_full = w_block | reg_full gives 1 at col9 on an empty FIFO. :188 reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_block & reg_full gives 0, because the write is treated as blocked. The RTL's own rule is consistent (blocked, so no pulse), but its block term has a third input that spec:527 does not have.
